title: Article 108 — Joint sitting of both Houses in certain cases

content.overview: Article 108 provides for a joint sitting of both Houses when a Bill (other than a Money Bill or a Bill for amending the Constitution) passed by one House is rejected by the other, or the Houses disagree on amendments, or more than six months elapse from receipt of the Bill by the other House without it being passed. The President may notify intention to summon a joint sitting unless the Bill has already lapsed by dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
content.glance: Joint sitting for ordinary Bills on rejection, disagreement on amendments, or 6+ months delay. Not for Money Bills or Constitution-amendment Bills. Presided by Speaker.
content.study:
Article 108 applies when:
- a Bill passed by one House is rejected by the other; or
- the Houses have finally disagreed as to amendments; or
- more than six months elapse from the date of receipt of the Bill by the other House without the Bill being passed by it.

The President may (unless the Bill has lapsed by dissolution of the Lok Sabha) notify an intention to summon the Houses to meet in a joint sitting. After such notification, neither House may proceed further with the Bill. At the joint sitting, the Bill (with agreed amendments, if any) is decided by a majority of the total number of members of both Houses present and voting.

Exclusions: Money Bills and Bills for amendment of the Constitution are outside joint-sitting procedure.

Presiding: Speaker of the Lok Sabha (or person acting as such).

Examination: three triggers; exclusion of Money Bills and Art 368 Bills; majority of both Houses present and voting; Speaker presides.

sections.heading: Triggers and exclusions
sections.body:
Triggers: rejection; final disagreement on amendments; more than six months without passage by the other House.
Exclusions: Money Bills; Constitution-amendment Bills.
Decision: majority of total members of both Houses present and voting at the joint sitting.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When can a joint sitting be summoned under Article 108?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 108, if a Bill (other than a Money Bill or a Constitution-amendment Bill) passed by one House is rejected by the other, or the Houses disagree on amendments, or more than six months elapse without the Bill being passed by the other House, the President may notify an intention to summon a joint sitting (unless the Bill has lapsed by dissolution of the Lok Sabha). The joint sitting decides by a majority of the members of both Houses present and voting.

examTips: Three triggers; no joint sitting for Money Bills or Art 368 Bills; Speaker presides.

keyTakeaways: Art 108: joint sitting for ordinary Bills on deadlock; not Money Bills or constitutional amendments.
